title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
authors: Miaojiang Chen, Wenjing Xiao, Haiqiang Chen, Jiarong Liang, Anfeng Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Saif Al-Kuwari, Ahmed Farouk, H. Herbert Song
problem: Storing half of an entangled probe in a quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn an unknown Pauli channel: without memory, identifying an \(n\)-qubit Pauli operator hidden in a channel takes \(\Omega(2^n)\) uses. Real memories are noisy. How much memory noise can the exponential advantage survive, and is there a sharp threshold?
result: For Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues \(\lambda_X,\lambda_Y,\lambda_Z\), the advantage is governed by \(\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2\). Every protocol whose probe is half of a maximally entangled state gains no exponential advantage when this sum is at most 1, and for general protocols the question reduces to the additivity of a Rényi-2 coherent information, which the authors verify numerically for up to four memory qubits and conjecture. Coded memories retain a growing advantage within 1% of the threshold. On the Wukong 180 superconducting processor, nine Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with size, reversing at \(a^*=0.636\) as a parameter-free model predicts, and a three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one.
significance: The threshold gives a single, hardware-measurable number that says whether a noisy memory still provides an exponential learning advantage, and the experiment places a real processor on that diagram. It also identifies a new additivity question for a Rényi-2 coherent information, distinct from the superadditive von Neumann quantity behind quantum capacity, and shows that a small code can beat the best uncoded strategy on present hardware for strongly biased noise.
limitations: The converse is proved for protocols with an entangled (maximally mixed memory) probe; for arbitrary protocols it rests on Conjecture 1, supported by numerics up to \(m\le4\) memory qubits and random stabilizer codes up to seven qubits. Protocols are assumed not to keep quantum data across uses, and only Pauli memory noise is treated. In the experiment, memory noise is injected as random Pauli gates; syndromes are read out at the end because the cloud service lacks mid-circuit measurement, and the coding gain changes sign once the noise bias drops below about \(\lambda_Z\approx0.96\). No AI-use statement appears in the version read; the acknowledgements were removed for anonymous review.

methods_basis: Based on the linked paper version. Derivations marked as editorial, and suggested uses in other problems, are editorial guidance rather than results of the paper.
description: The task is to identify an unknown \(n\)-qubit Pauli operator \(P\), drawn uniformly, from uses of the channel \(\Lambda_P(\rho)=(I+\mathrm{tr}(P\rho)P)/2^n\). In each round the learner prepares the system together with an \(m\)-qubit memory, sends the system through \(\Lambda_P\) while each memory qubit suffers a Pauli channel with eigenvalues \(\mathbf{\lambda}\), and measures both. Without memory the task needs \(\Omega(2^n)\) uses; with a perfect memory and Bell probes it needs only polynomially many.

The per-use information is bounded through the \(\chi^2\) divergence between outcome distributions, which is at most \((2^nK-1)/(4^n-1)\) with \(K=2^{-\widetilde H_2^{\downarrow}(R|A)}\), a sandwiched Rényi-2 conditional entropy of the probe after memory noise. An exponential advantage requires \(K\) to grow exponentially. For probes whose memory marginal is maximally mixed, \(K=\kappa^m\) with \(\kappa=(1+\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2)/2\), so no advantage grows when \(\sum\lambda^2\le1\).

For Bell sampling the advantage is a product of per-site factors \(2\mu_j\), where \(\mu_j\) is the geometric mean of four letter factors \(G_I=1,G_X,G_Y,G_Z\) (squared visibilities). The converse instead involves their arithmetic mean, and better measurement frames and codes move protocols from the geometric toward the arithmetic mean. Codes of distance 2 to 4 with syndrome-aware decoding grow down to depolarizing fidelity \(\eta=0.58\), within 1% of the threshold \(1/\sqrt3\).

On Wukong 180, nine disjoint Bell pairs (18 qubits) with injected dephasing \((a,a,1)\) show a joint advantage linear in the number of sites, with a slope that changes sign at \(a^*=0.636\), matching the prediction \(0.5/0.786\) from independently measured noiseless factors. Joint statistics factorize across sites, and a three-qubit phase-flip code, end to end, turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one over a range of \(a\).

methods.technique: A Rényi-2 bound on what one use of the channel can reveal
methods.explanation: To show that a noisy memory gives no exponential advantage, one must bound the information about \(P\) extracted per channel use by any measurement. A \(\chi^2\) divergence averaged over \(P\) reduces, after Pauli twirling, to a single collision quantity of the probe state, which can then be computed for each memory noise.
math: Averaging the outcome distribution over a uniformly random Pauli \(P\) and comparing with the completely depolarizing channel, the mean \(\chi^2\) divergence per use is at most \((2^nK-1)/(4^n-1)\) with \(K=2^{-\widetilde H_2^{\downarrow}(R|A)_\rho}\). For \(K\le1\) this is the memoryless value \(1/(2^n+1)\), so \(\Omega(2^n)\) uses are needed.

For a probe whose memory half is maximally mixed, each memory qubit contributes independently and \(K=\kappa^m\) with \(\kappa=(1+\sum\lambda^2)/2\). Editorial derivation of the collision-entropy reading: a Pauli channel with eigenvalues \(\lambda\) applies Pauli \(a\) with probability \(p_a=\tfrac14(1\pm\lambda_X\pm\lambda_Y\pm\lambda_Z)\), so \[2\sum_ap_a^2=\tfrac12\Bigl(1+\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2\Bigr)=\kappa.\] The threshold \(\kappa=1\) is where the memory error has collision entropy exactly one bit. Editorial check: both sides equal \(1.25\) for \(\lambda=(0.5,0.5,1)\) and \(1.04\) for \(\lambda=(0.6,0.6,0.6)\).

For depolarizing noise \(\lambda=(\eta,\eta,\eta)\), \(\kappa=1\) gives \(\eta=1/\sqrt3\approx0.577\). Bell sampling has per-site factor \(\mu=\eta^{3/2}\) and grows only for \(\eta>2^{-2/3}\approx0.630\), where \(\sum\lambda^2=1.19\); the gap between \(0.577\) and \(0.630\) is what codes and memory frames can close.
methods.transfer: Bounding the per-use information by a collision (Rényi-2) entropy of the probe turns a question about all adaptive learning strategies into a question about a single state. The same reduction applies to other learning tasks where averaging over a group twirl makes the divergence depend only on a second moment.

methods.technique: Placing a processor on the threshold diagram from letter factors
methods.explanation: Hardware adds its own noise on top of the injected memory noise, so it is not obvious where a real device sits relative to the threshold. For Bell probes the three letter factors are squared effective Pauli eigenvalues of the whole site, so their sum measures the effective \(\sum\lambda^2\) directly, processor errors included.
math: For ideal Bell pairs under dephasing \((a,a,1)\), the letter factors are \(a^2,a^2,1\) and the per-site factor is \(\mu=(1\cdot a^2\cdot a^2\cdot1)^{1/4}=a\). If the processor multiplies each site's factor by a constant \(\mu_j(1)\), measured on interleaved noiseless circuits, then \(\mu_j(a)=\mu_j(1)\,a\), and the advantage \(\prod_j2\mu_j\) changes from shrinking to growing at \(a^*=1/(2\mu(1))\). Editorial check: with the measured geometric mean \(\mu(1)=0.786\), \(a^*=0.636\), the value observed.

Because \(\Sigma_j=G_X+G_Y+G_Z\) includes errors on the system qubit, it is a lower bound on the memory's own \(\sum\lambda^2\). Every measured site obeys \(\mu_j\le(1+\Sigma_j)/4\), the arithmetic-mean bound. Five settings bring \(\bar\Sigma\) below 1, and in all of them the joint advantage shrinks with size, as the theory requires.

In the best memory frame, a rotation equalizes the three visibilities at \(\sum\lambda/3\), giving \(\mu=((1+2a)/3)^{3/2}\) for dephasing. Editorial check: this equals \(1/2\) at \(a=(3\cdot2^{-2/3}-1)/2=0.445\), as stated; the three-qubit code on hardware stays above this ideal best-frame curve at all twelve settings with \(a\le0.64\).
methods.transfer: Measuring squared effective Pauli eigenvalues per site gives a direct, model-light estimate of where a device stands relative to an information-theoretic threshold. The approach can benchmark memories for other entanglement-assisted protocols, such as sensing and channel estimation.
